title: Balanced Brackets Check (Stack Operations)
real_world_story: A code editor must highlight bracket mistakes instantly. Every time a player or programmer types a formula with (), [] and {}, the validator must decide whether all brackets open and close in the correct order.

real_world_connection.input_represents: A bracket string typed by the user
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Pushing openers on a stack and popping on closers to check nesting

problem_statement: Given a string s containing only the characters '(', ')', '{', '}', '[' and ']', determine whether the bracket sequence is valid. A sequence is valid when every opener is closed by the same bracket type in the correct nested order.
task: Return 1 if the bracket sequence is valid, otherwise 0.
input_format: A single line containing the bracket string s. The line may be empty, which means an empty sequence.
output_format: Print 1 if the sequence is valid, otherwise 0.

examples.explanation: Each opener is closed by the matching closer in order, so the sequence is valid.
'(' was closed by ']' instead of ')', so the sequence is invalid.

expected_algorithm.name: Stack Operations
expected_algorithm.reason: Openers are pushed and each closer must pop the matching opener, which is exactly last-in-first-out stack validation.

hint: Push every opener onto a stack.
On a closer, the stack must be non-empty and its top must match.
The sequence is valid only when the stack is empty at the end.
real_world_takeaway: Stacks validate nested puzzle and code structures in one linear pass.
